we propose a novel approach for extracting foreground/background masks from networks pre- trained for the task of image recognition, and show that these masks are useful for weakly-supervised multi-class semantic segmentation, yielding state-of-the-art results.

we can extract accurate foreground/background and multi-class masks from networks pre- trained for object recognition, and that using them in conjunction with a tag-based weakly supervised training loss yields state of the art results for tag-based weakly- supervised semantic segmentation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show how to obtain accurate object masks from networks pre-train for object recognition and how to use them in conjunction with a novel weakly-supervised learning loss to achieve state-of-the-art weakly-supervised segmentation results.
we show how to obtain accurate masks for semantic segmentation from a pre-trained object recognition network.
we are the first to show how to extract object masks from pre-trained networks and that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art weakly-supervised methods on semantic segmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information encoded in the activations of a network can be used in a principled manner to extract useful priors for semantic segmentation.
the information contained in a network pre-trained for object recognition can be exploited to generate masks, which in turn are useful in weakly-supervised segmentation.
the information extracted from a pre-trained network is enough for obtaining good masks, which can then be used to improve semantic segmentation results in a weakly supervised setting.
